label: PRNN Lecture 01 — Introduction
locator_basis: one-based PDF page index; printed slide numbers differ after page 44

concepts.target: Four AI perspectives; human/rational and thinking/acting distinctions, rational action, Turing-test purpose and limitations, cognitive versus logical approaches.
Breadth of AI applications/subfields with economical examples; capability is distinct from reliable deployment.
AI, learning from examples, and multilayer neural learning are related but not interchangeable; explicit rules versus learned behavior.
Rule knowledge, facts, inference and explanation/user interface roles; representative classic AI applications.
Hand-designed features versus learned representations; hierarchical simple-to-complex features and end-to-end flow.
Data/compute/problem complexity tradeoffs, scaling curves and limits of generality; illustrations are not universal guarantees.
Historical expectation/adoption context, condensed rather than copying successive charts or treating them as current benchmark evidence.
Label cost, rare-pattern and viewpoint coverage, biased datasets and possible mitigation without claiming guarantees.
Adversarial perturbations/training, context sensitivity, combinatorial variation, compositionality and testing difficulty.
Visual reasoning limitations and unintended optimization/fitness outcomes; terse source items still require teaching.
Four learning families distinguished by available supervision, inputs, outputs, and feedback.
Labels, input-to-output learning, error as a discrepancy, and conditional probability notation with symbols explained.
Data preparation, informative shape features, classifier training and reuse at testing; grayscale does not imply binary.
Unlabeled input structure/density perspective, clustering examples and distinction from supervised labels; handle ambiguous nearest-neighbor wording accurately.
Initialization, nearest-center assignment, mean update and repetition, within-cluster variation, restarts, and elbow selection of cluster count.
Co-occurrence/dependency rules and their purpose; named association methods need concise recognition, not invented detailed coursework.
Few labels plus abundant unlabeled examples, predict-label/retrain loop and convergence; distinguish illustrative loop from a universal algorithm.
Agent, environment, state, actions and reward feedback cycle versus fixed target labels.
Measurements/patterns, recognition applications, variability, OCR meaning and context-dependent performance rather than universal accuracy claims.
Input-to-output function approximation; discrete class prediction versus numerical quantity prediction.
Binary image example, informative features, per-column black-pixel count and maximum feature, with symbols/interpretation and a usable calculation.
Training feature distributions/histograms, class-conditional density interpretation, threshold boundary, overlap/variability and classification error; posterior is not the same object as likelihood.
Additional useful features create multidimensional feature space and separating line/plane; qualified error-reduction claim.
Cover context may be retained; contact details, grading, email rules, bibliography/acknowledgments normally omitted or condensed without losing instructional foundations.
